The Parallelogram Law

An identity hides between the two diagonals and the two sides of a parallelogram. This scene slides the exponent ppp and checks when that identity survives.

Every norm that comes from an inner product satisfies the identity. Computing with e1e_1e1​ and e2e_2e2​ makes the left side 2⋅22/p2 \cdot 2^{2/p}2⋅22/p and the right side 444. The two agree only at p=2p = 2p=2. So an ℓp\ell^pℓp norm with ppp different from 2 cannot come from any inner product.

For example, a 📐 parallelogram drawn with a ruler stays exactly the same, but the measuring ruler is swapped. If swapping the ruler alone breaks the diagonal identity, that ruler never came from an inner-product blueprint.

∥x+y∥2+∥x−y∥2=2∥x∥2+2∥y∥2\|x+y\|^2 + \|x-y\|^2 = 2\|x\|^2 + 2\|y\|^2∥x+y∥2+∥x−y∥2=2∥x∥2+2∥y∥2
⟨x,y⟩=∥x+y∥2−∥x−y∥24\langle x, y \rangle = \frac{\|x+y\|^2 - \|x-y\|^2}{4}⟨x,y⟩=4∥x+y∥2−∥x−y∥2​

Examples & Exercises

Prove completely that in a real inner product space, every x,yx, yx,y satisfies the parallelogram law ∥x+y∥2+∥x−y∥2=2∥x∥2+2∥y∥2\|x+y\|^2 + \|x-y\|^2 = 2\|x\|^2 + 2\|y\|^2∥x+y∥2+∥x−y∥2=2∥x∥2+2∥y∥2.

∥x+y∥2+∥x−y∥2=2∥x∥2+2∥y∥2\|x+y\|^2 + \|x-y\|^2 = 2\|x\|^2 + 2\|y\|^2∥x+y∥2+∥x−y∥2=2∥x∥2+2∥y∥2
Show proof

  1. Expand the norm of the sum through the inner product. In a real inner product space ∥x+y∥2=⟨x+y,x+y⟩\|x+y\|^2 = \langle x+y, x+y \rangle∥x+y∥2=⟨x+y,x+y⟩, and bilinearity with symmetry gives ⟨x+y,x+y⟩=⟨x,x⟩+⟨x,y⟩+⟨y,x⟩+⟨y,y⟩=∥x∥2+2⟨x,y⟩+∥y∥2\langle x+y, x+y \rangle = \langle x, x \rangle + \langle x, y \rangle + \langle y, x \rangle + \langle y, y \rangle = \|x\|^2 + 2\langle x, y \rangle + \|y\|^2⟨x+y,x+y⟩=⟨x,x⟩+⟨x,y⟩+⟨y,x⟩+⟨y,y⟩=∥x∥2+2⟨x,y⟩+∥y∥2. That is, ∥x+y∥2=∥x∥2+2⟨x,y⟩+∥y∥2\|x+y\|^2 = \|x\|^2 + 2\langle x, y \rangle + \|y\|^2∥x+y∥2=∥x∥2+2⟨x,y⟩+∥y∥2.

  2. Expand the norm of the difference the same way. ∥x−y∥2=⟨x−y,x−y⟩=⟨x,x⟩−⟨x,y⟩−⟨y,x⟩+⟨y,y⟩=∥x∥2−2⟨x,y⟩+∥y∥2\|x-y\|^2 = \langle x-y, x-y \rangle = \langle x, x \rangle - \langle x, y \rangle - \langle y, x \rangle + \langle y, y \rangle = \|x\|^2 - 2\langle x, y \rangle + \|y\|^2∥x−y∥2=⟨x−y,x−y⟩=⟨x,x⟩−⟨x,y⟩−⟨y,x⟩+⟨y,y⟩=∥x∥2−2⟨x,y⟩+∥y∥2. That is, ∥x−y∥2=∥x∥2−2⟨x,y⟩+∥y∥2\|x-y\|^2 = \|x\|^2 - 2\langle x, y \rangle + \|y\|^2∥x−y∥2=∥x∥2−2⟨x,y⟩+∥y∥2.

  3. Add the two identities. The cross terms cancel: ∥x+y∥2+∥x−y∥2=(∥x∥2+2⟨x,y⟩+∥y∥2)+(∥x∥2−2⟨x,y⟩+∥y∥2)=2∥x∥2+2∥y∥2\|x+y\|^2 + \|x-y\|^2 = \left(\|x\|^2 + 2\langle x, y \rangle + \|y\|^2\right) + \left(\|x\|^2 - 2\langle x, y \rangle + \|y\|^2\right) = 2\|x\|^2 + 2\|y\|^2∥x+y∥2+∥x−y∥2=(∥x∥2+2⟨x,y⟩+∥y∥2)+(∥x∥2−2⟨x,y⟩+∥y∥2)=2∥x∥2+2∥y∥2. This is the parallelogram law, and the proof is complete.

  4. Remark: this is the real case. The law itself also holds in complex inner product spaces by the same expansion, but the polarization identity in problem 3 below changes to a form using Re\mathrm{Re}Re there — not needed here.

For e1=(1,0)e_1 = (1,0)e1​=(1,0) and e2=(0,1)e_2 = (0,1)e2​=(0,1) in ℓp(R2)\ell^p(\mathbb{R}^2)ℓp(R2), compute both sides of the parallelogram law and prove completely that equality holds only when p=2p = 2p=2. Conclude that for p≠2p \ne 2p=2 the ℓp\ell^pℓp norm is not induced by any inner product.

∥e1+e2∥p2+∥e1−e2∥p2=21+2/p,2∥e1∥p2+2∥e2∥p2=4=22\|e_1+e_2\|_p^2 + \|e_1-e_2\|_p^2 = 2^{1 + 2/p}, \qquad 2\|e_1\|_p^2 + 2\|e_2\|_p^2 = 4 = 2^2∥e1​+e2​∥p2​+∥e1​−e2​∥p2​=21+2/p,2∥e1​∥p2​+2∥e2​∥p2​=4=22
Show proof

  1. Compute each norm first. Since e1+e2=(1,1)e_1 + e_2 = (1,1)e1​+e2​=(1,1), ∥e1+e2∥p=(∣1∣p+∣1∣p)1/p=21/p\|e_1+e_2\|_p = \left(|1|^p + |1|^p\right)^{1/p} = 2^{1/p}∥e1​+e2​∥p​=(∣1∣p+∣1∣p)1/p=21/p, and squaring gives ∥e1+e2∥p2=(21/p)2=22/p\|e_1+e_2\|_p^2 = \left(2^{1/p}\right)^2 = 2^{2/p}∥e1​+e2​∥p2​=(21/p)2=22/p. Likewise e1−e2=(1,−1)e_1 - e_2 = (1,-1)e1​−e2​=(1,−1), so ∥e1−e2∥p=(∣1∣p+∣−1∣p)1/p=21/p\|e_1-e_2\|_p = \left(|1|^p + |-1|^p\right)^{1/p} = 2^{1/p}∥e1​−e2​∥p​=(∣1∣p+∣−1∣p)1/p=21/p and ∥e1−e2∥p2=22/p\|e_1-e_2\|_p^2 = 2^{2/p}∥e1​−e2​∥p2​=22/p.

  2. Collect both sides. The left side is ∥e1+e2∥p2+∥e1−e2∥p2=22/p+22/p=2⋅22/p=21+2/p\|e_1+e_2\|_p^2 + \|e_1-e_2\|_p^2 = 2^{2/p} + 2^{2/p} = 2 \cdot 2^{2/p} = 2^{1 + 2/p}∥e1​+e2​∥p2​+∥e1​−e2​∥p2​=22/p+22/p=2⋅22/p=21+2/p. Meanwhile ∥e1∥p=∥e2∥p=1\|e_1\|_p = \|e_2\|_p = 1∥e1​∥p​=∥e2​∥p​=1, so the right side is 2∥e1∥p2+2∥e2∥p2=2⋅1+2⋅1=4=222\|e_1\|_p^2 + 2\|e_2\|_p^2 = 2 \cdot 1 + 2 \cdot 1 = 4 = 2^22∥e1​∥p2​+2∥e2​∥p2​=2⋅1+2⋅1=4=22. Hence equality is equivalent to 21+2/p=222^{1 + 2/p} = 2^221+2/p=22.

  3. (⇒)(\Rightarrow)(⇒) Suppose equality 21+2/p=222^{1 + 2/p} = 2^221+2/p=22 holds. The map t↦2tt \mapsto 2^tt↦2t is injective, so the exponents must agree: 1+2/p=21 + 2/p = 21+2/p=2. Hence 2/p=12/p = 12/p=1, i.e. p=2p = 2p=2.

  4. (⇐)(\Leftarrow)(⇐) Conversely, suppose p=2p = 2p=2. Then 1+2/p=1+1=21 + 2/p = 1 + 1 = 21+2/p=1+1=2, so the left side is 21+2/p=22=42^{1 + 2/p} = 2^2 = 421+2/p=22=4, directly equal to the right side 444. Hence equality holds.

  5. Conclusion: for p≠2p \ne 2p=2 the ℓp\ell^pℓp norm violates the parallelogram law. Since problem 1 shows that every inner-product norm satisfies the law, by the Jordan-von Neumann theorem the ℓp\ell^pℓp norm for p≠2p \ne 2p=2 is not induced by any inner product.

Verify completely that in a real inner product space the polarization identity ⟨x,y⟩=∥x+y∥2−∥x−y∥24\langle x, y \rangle = \frac{\|x+y\|^2 - \|x-y\|^2}{4}⟨x,y⟩=4∥x+y∥2−∥x−y∥2​ holds.

⟨x,y⟩=∥x+y∥2−∥x−y∥24\langle x, y \rangle = \frac{\|x+y\|^2 - \|x-y\|^2}{4}⟨x,y⟩=4∥x+y∥2−∥x−y∥2​
Show proof

  1. Reuse the expansions from problem 1: ∥x+y∥2=∥x∥2+2⟨x,y⟩+∥y∥2\|x+y\|^2 = \|x\|^2 + 2\langle x, y \rangle + \|y\|^2∥x+y∥2=∥x∥2+2⟨x,y⟩+∥y∥2 and ∥x−y∥2=∥x∥2−2⟨x,y⟩+∥y∥2\|x-y\|^2 = \|x\|^2 - 2\langle x, y \rangle + \|y\|^2∥x−y∥2=∥x∥2−2⟨x,y⟩+∥y∥2.

  2. Subtract the two identities. The ∥x∥2\|x\|^2∥x∥2 and ∥y∥2\|y\|^2∥y∥2 terms disappear and only the cross terms survive: ∥x+y∥2−∥x−y∥2=(∥x∥2+2⟨x,y⟩+∥y∥2)−(∥x∥2−2⟨x,y⟩+∥y∥2)=4⟨x,y⟩\|x+y\|^2 - \|x-y\|^2 = \left(\|x\|^2 + 2\langle x, y \rangle + \|y\|^2\right) - \left(\|x\|^2 - 2\langle x, y \rangle + \|y\|^2\right) = 4\langle x, y \rangle∥x+y∥2−∥x−y∥2=(∥x∥2+2⟨x,y⟩+∥y∥2)−(∥x∥2−2⟨x,y⟩+∥y∥2)=4⟨x,y⟩.

  3. Divide both sides by 444: ∥x+y∥2−∥x−y∥24=⟨x,y⟩\frac{\|x+y\|^2 - \|x-y\|^2}{4} = \langle x, y \rangle4∥x+y∥2−∥x−y∥2​=⟨x,y⟩ — the polarization identity is verified. The inner product is completely determined by the norm alone.

  4. By the Jordan-von Neumann theorem, whenever a norm satisfies the parallelogram law, this very formula defines an inner product for it (statement only).
